newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher on March CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher on March CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday following a higher than expected March consumer price index (CPI) and unaffected by a corruption scandal that could threaten Israel's government. Indices:
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.09 pct to 105.28
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 to 104.12

"Because of the higher than expected CPI, for the first time in months there was surplus demand for CPI-linked bonds," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities. "The feeling is that inflation is not going down and maybe even rising."
The March CPI released on Tuesday after the markets had closed posted a higher than expected 1.0 percent rise. Analysts' expectations were for a 0.7-0.8 percent rise.
Prices of CPI-linked bonds rose across the board with the main rises in short-term bonds, Halpern said.
Traders said the bond market had been unaffected by media reports that police had recommended corruption charges against men close to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Because of the high CPI there were surplus supplies for unlinked bonds that caused the prices to fall slightly," said a trader. Prices of unlinked bonds had been rising because of expectations that inflation was on its way down.

Prices of the dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower after days of rises due to the strengthning of the dollar worldwide. "The shekel appreciated slightly today, so there was probably some profit taking," said Halpern.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
